title: Data leakage: the ways it gets in, and how it looks in the metrics

videos.script: Add one column to the churn model, and its score jumps. {{jump}} Point nine five, where the honest model gets point eight. Two and a half times the money. {{money}} The column is called days since last order. It sounds exactly right. And it was computed on the day the file was exported. Not on the day of the prediction. {{export}} For somebody who left in 2024, it counts the days until 2026. Nobody could have known that in 2024. {{future}} Split the data by time, and the same model is worth nothing at all. {{zero}} That is leakage. Information in the training data that will not exist when the model is used. {{definition}} This lesson shows four ways it gets in. A column that is the answer. A column from the future. A preparation step fitted on every row. And a split with relatives on both sides. {{four}} No score can prove a column innocent. So the lesson ends with a habit. Before a column goes in, somebody says where it comes from. {{end}}
